newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures slide again, Nymex holds steady.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures slide again, Nymex holds steady.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures continued their fall on Thursday to post fresh nine-month lows, ignoring NYMEX's WTI contract which traded steady in early pit business, brokers said.

May Brent fell to a morning low of $18.26, 25 cents off Wednesday's settlement price before recovering mildly. But it slumped again in late afternoon, as volume picked up, to hit a new bottom of $18.07. By 1645 GMT it had risen again to $18.20.
"Brent has got a mind of its own at the moment," said one broker. "We saw it move down, then the volume piled in."
May WTI opened at $19.55 and bobbed around that level.
London brokers had expected it to blip up before continuing Wednesday's slide.
April IPE gas oil closed $3.50 down in quiet trade, posting less of a loss than predicted. Much of the decline came in the last half hour of trade.
"Nothing really went on, it was a pretty boring day in a market looking for headlines," said one gas oil futures broker. He saw little change on Friday with further falls and thin activity.
Thursday's fall in May Brent took the spot contract to its lowest since June 25th last year.
That price was a recovery from the previous day's $17.95, a number some traders spoke of as the next target.
"It's an evil market, it's not trending and not holding support, it's just bearish," said one broker.
